parsed.explanation: The quote is verbatim and the objection reads it correctly. §3 proves only that V contains at most one *positive* number (its argument starts "Suppose V contains two distinct positive numbers c1 > c2 > 0"). Nothing in the write-up excludes negative values of g: the only constraint recorded is "g(x) > -x", which permits g(x)=a<0 at individual points. Hence "V ⊆ {0,c}" (and the exhaustive split S_0 ∪ S_c = R_{>0} used in §6) does not follow. The needed lemma d(t) ≥ 0 for all t (rubric item S) is proved nowhere in the text; the objector's repair — iterating (4) gives g(x+na)=a and x+na>0 for all n, impossible for a<0 — is correct but absent. Since §§4–7 rest on the two-value dichotomy, the necessity argument is incomplete as written.
